text:
Aisha Patel: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a Console flow to surface per-tenant SLO alerts and routing. Goal: let product/platform teams set tenant-scoped notification routing, quiet windows, and noise filters without touching org-level SLOs. Thoughts?

Marco Nguyen: Love the idea. Two quick asks: 1) can routing map to tenant-specific escalation channels (PagerDuty/team Slack)? 2) how do we avoid alert storms when a single customer spikes briefly?

Riley Chen: Agree. We should differentiate burn-rate vs absolute-threshold alerts. Small tenants can blow burn-rate easily; suggest a min-volume gate (only alert if traffic or error volume > threshold).

Aisha Patel: Yup — prototype includes gating rules: require either tokens/sec > 50 OR errors/min > 5 before firing tenant alert. Also a "snooze scope" (tenant-only / org-wide) option.

Marco Nguyen: Can you paste the prototype config?

Aisha Patel: Sure — config sketch: ```json
{"tenant_id": "t-123", "alerts": [{"name": "latency-slo-breach", "condition": {"burn_rate": 3, "min_volume_tokens_per_sec": 50}, "routing": {"slack_channel": "#tenant-ops-t123", "pagerduty_service": "svc-ops-tenant-123"}, "snooze_window": {"start": "22:00", "end": "06:00", "tz": "UTC"}}] }
```

deploy-bot: Reminder: the global paging bridge requires a team mapping entry or it will drop the external routing (we get a lot of lost pages otherwise).

Sam (ops): Strong +1 for conservative defaults and min-volume gating. Also add a "dry-run" toggle in the UI to preview who would be notified (helpful before enabling).

Riley Chen: Also expose an "alert noise" metric per-tenant (alerts per 1k requests) so product can see churn and we can suggest smaller thresholds or better rate-limits. This ties into Optimize recommendations.

Aisha Patel: Plan: I'll open a prototype PR with API + UI mock and a small backend guard. API idea: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/alerting with the JSON shape above. UI: add "Tenant alerts" card on SLOs page with routing, quiet windows, and dry-run. ETA: EOD Friday, will tag reviewers.

Marco Nguyen: Quick Q — should we support a special "maintenance" suppression label so customers' dev ops can silence alerts during planned upgrades?

Riley Chen: Yes — label + automatic expiry (auto-resolve when window ends) is ideal. Also persist the reason field for audit.

Aisha Patel: Action items: 1) Aisha: PR + mocks. 2) Marco: auth/mapping doc for external routing. 3) Sam: propose default threshold set. I'll add a sample dataset for noise metrics. :thumbsup:

Marco Nguyen: SGTM. Thanks Aisha.

Sam (ops): Ping me once dry-run is wired, I'll run it against a couple tenants.
